# Connection

> Connection lets AI clients use approved external services without receiving the user's provider credentials.

## Install in Codex

Connection is a remote Streamable HTTP MCP server. When a user asks you to install Connection in Codex, explain the commands before running them. Installation and login require the user's explicit participation.

```bash
codex mcp add connection --url __CONNECTION_ORIGIN__/mcp
codex mcp login connection --scopes mcp --oauth-client-registration dcr
```

The login command opens Connection's OAuth flow. The user signs in to Connection in the browser. Never ask the user to paste an LDAP password, Connection access token, or provider credential into chat or Codex configuration. After the company OAuth callback, the user clicks “完成公司登录” before LDAP login. Admission lasts 30 minutes; LDAP remains the business identity and may require its own login; existing connections and grants are retained.

On deployments with company entrance protection, the browser first completes direct company OAuth admission, then Connection LDAP login. The LDAP account remains the business identity; the two accounts need not match. Existing connections/grants remain owned by that LDAP account. MCP, metadata, DCR and token/refresh/revoke calls continue using their existing protocols without company admission cookies or an extra apiKey. Never add company headers/cookies as a workaround for a machine 401. If browser entrance admission expires, reopen the console and complete admission before explicitly retrying; do not automatically replay a submitted operation. Signing out of Connection does not sign out of company SSO or clear the admission proof.


Installing and logging in do not grant access to GitHub, Jira, Confluence, or other providers. The user must connect a provider account and explicitly approve the Codex grant in Connection before provider actions become available. Company approval is off by default for existing and new Providers; users connect their own accounts directly unless an administrator enables approval for that Provider. When enabled, obtain valid company eligibility first. Follow the current Connections page; do not assume missing access always requires company approval. Shared-account eligibility is separate.

## Public URLs

`AUTHORIZED` only confirms admission, not successful execution or absence of submission. Preserve the original write idempotency key. Deterministic Provider rejection is `FAILED`; transport or terminal-persistence failure is unknown and must be reconciled before resubmission. These states alone do not require reauthorization.

- Installation guide: __CONNECTION_ORIGIN__/connection
- Connection console: __CONNECTION_ORIGIN__/connection/connections
- MCP endpoint: __CONNECTION_ORIGIN__/mcp

Do not infer additional endpoints, credentials, identities, grants, or permissions from this file.

## Newly published Provider capabilities

New capabilities require explicit Consumer consent. Candidates are bounded by the published catalog, Consumer declaration and company approval, not the saved external scope snapshot. Consent permits client use; the Provider determines actual operation permissions. Scope changes do not pause grants. Permission failures affect the operation only; recovery does not require repeat Consumer consent. Genuine credential expiry or revocation still requires reconnect. Healthy accounts have no persistent permission-refresh button. Only server-indicated upgrade or reconnect states expose recovery actions; new Actions or external scope changes do not require account updates. New-capability notices exclude old unchecked catalog Actions. Never collect credentials in chat or silently grant new Actions.

## Rehoboam release failure handoff

For final delivery or another Iris build, READ `get_release_family_continuation` for the remaining steps and template-controlled next-version suggestion. Use existing preview/confirm replacement with the current member id, then initialize the new member. Preserve Native and old records; explicitly select new upstream results for downstream retries, never copy old bound URLs into new requests. Suggestions do not reserve versions. Final-notice receipts, not Job success, establish completed delivery.

A releaser does not need to declare whether they have a local SDK checkout. Diagnose through authorized tools, then hand source changes to project developers unless the user explicitly requests them. All release-family stages (Jobs, manual PR, tests/results, decisions and delivery) support explicitly authorized Provider v14 `record_release_family_repair`. Generic resolved handling requires a validation link; source compilation needs PR, full commit SHA and CI evidence. This is operator-reported progress, not task completion; it never advances, changes Job outcomes or sends messages. When a Job is ready for verification, show results and explain remaining confirmation/delivery steps, then ask whether to continue. Read current family revision/template signature before recording and read back uncertain outcomes before retrying.

## GitHub Actions Job logs

When the current catalog exposes `github.get_workflow_job_logs`, it requires separate explicit Consumer consent. Discover it and read its guide before calling; obtain the Job ID through `github.list_workflow_run_jobs`. Follow `nextStartLine` for another page. A truncated response is not the full log; when `scanLimitReached` is true and `nextStartLine` is null, direct the user to the GitHub Actions log. Reading never reruns a build. Raw build logs may enter the authorized consumer/model context; authorize only appropriate logs. See [GitHub help](__CONNECTION_ORIGIN__/connection/help?chapter=15) for defaults, limits and recovery.
